https://www.dw.com/en/marine-one-helicop.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5INLL The White House said President Trump was never in harm's way Image: Eric Lee/REUTERS Advertisement The United States Federal Aviation Administration on Wednesday said it is investigating why a passenger jet was allowed to take off from Reagan Washington National Airport just as President Donald Trump's helicopter, Marine One, was approaching on Tuesday afternoon, in an apparent breach of safety rules adopted after last year's deadly midair collision near the airport. In January 2025, a collision between an American Airlines jet and an Army helicopter near Reagan National killed 67 people and led to tighter separation rules and radar-based tracking requirements. What do we know? Marine One lifted off from near the White House around 2:33 p.m. local time, headed to Joint Base Andrews ahead of a trip to Los Angeles. Reuters cited a source saying the jet involved was Envoy Air Flight 3742, an American Airlines regional jet bound for Pensacola, Florida, which departed a minute later. A second flight, Republic 4700, was rerouted as a precaution after coming within three miles (about 4.8 kilometers) of the airport. The jet was climbing above Marine One, so the two were never on a collision course. "Based on our preliminary safety review, there was momentary loss of separation after which the ​aircraft continued to move away from one another," the FAA said on Wednesday. FAA rules require aircraft near airports to stay at least 1.5 miles apart horizontally and 500 feet apart vertically. Both aircraft landed safely. White House says president was not in danger "Marine One flights are piloted by some of the best aviators in the world, and at no point was the President in harm's way," White House spokesperson Kush Desai said in a statement. The Marine Corps defended the helicopter pilots' actions. "There were no 'close calls' with the routine Marine One movement," Marine Corps spokesperson Capt. Jacob Sugg said in an email to the Associated Press. Under rules adopted after last year's crash, Reagan National is supposed to pause takeoffs and landings whenever a helicopter is on a conflicting route. But sources told Reuters controllers did not halt commercial flights on Tuesday as required. The National Transportation Safety Board said it would investigate, and the FAA said it plans to convene its own safety review. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/08/kdnp.text: Menü Kereső A KDNP szerint Baka András Magyar Péterhez hasonlóan bosszút akar állni a Fideszen Belföld Nádor András Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Baka András korábban nemzetközi bírói fórumokig is elment, hogy bebizonyítsa, nem lehet a határozott időre kinevezett közjogi vezetőket a ciklus közben elmozdítani” – írta a KDNP frakcióvezetője a Facebookon a Tisza szombaton bejelentett köztársaságielnök-jelöltjéről . Rétvári Bence szerint Baka úgy ülhet be Sulyok Tamás székébe, hogy utóbbit a ciklusa közben, ráadásul „jogsértő és erőszakos módon” mozdították el . A frakcióvezető a posztban ezzel szemben annyit írt Baka 2011-es elmozdításáról, hogy az „azért történt meg, mert megszűnt a Legfelsőbb Bíróság, amit irányított”. Rétvári szerint akárcsak Magyar Péter, Baka András is bosszút akar állni a Fideszen, perben és haragban állt az előző kormánnyal. „Egyéni sértettség van bennük, és ez motiválja őket.” Az kétségtelen, hogy a Tisza szombaton bejelentett jelöltje perben állt az előző kormánnyal. Csakhogy Rétvári arról nem írt, hogy 2016 júniusában Baka jogerősen is pert nyert Strasbourgban az akkori Orbán-kormány ellen. A bíróság megállapította, hogy a főbírót jogellenesen, személyre szabott jogalkotással menesztették idő előtt a tisztségéből. Az ítélet szerint azért, mert szakmai minőségében nyilvánosan kritizálta a bíróságok függetlenségét veszélyeztető lépéseket. Nem bontotta ki az igazság minden részletét Rétvári azzal sem, hogy csak annyit írt Baka 2011-es elmozdításáról, hogy az azért történt, mert megszűnt a Legfelsőbb Bíróság. A Legfelsőbb Bíróság, amit akkor Baka vezetett, valóban megszűnt. De nem magától, hanem azért, mert a Fidesz–KDNP-s kétharmaddal működő parlament átnevezte a Legfelsőbb Bíróságot Kúriára, az elnök megbízatása pedig, ellentétben az összes többi bírói kinevezéssel, lejárt. https://news.webindia123.com/news/Articl.text: Ulle Madise elected as President of Estonia As per TASS, the members of Estonias Riigikogu parliament elected Madise as the president of the Baltic country via secret ballot. It was reported that while 71 lawmakers voted for Madise, seven did not support her candidacy. Madise was the lone candidate in the election. Alar Karis, who had led the country since 2021, did not seek a second term for personal reasons, TASS said. Estonias parliament conducts its election for the president by secret ballot. The candidates for head of state must be Estonian citizens by birth and at least 40 years old. To win the presidency, a candidate must secure more than two-thirds of lawmakers votes, or at least 68 votes, TASS reported. Madise, 51, is a lawyer who holds a doctorate in law. She previously worked at the Justice Ministry and the parliaments Constitutional Committee, and served as a legal adviser to the president and dealt with constitutional review matters. Since 2015, she has served as Chancellor of Justice, an independent official overseeing the legality of the legislative and executive branches. TASS reported that representatives of the Conservative Peoples Party of Estonia challenged the legality of her eligibility to run, arguing that combining the posts of Chancellor of Justice and presidential candidate violated the separation of powers. The Supreme Court, Estonias highest judicial authority, rejected the complaint, it said. In a post on X, Estonias ex-president Alar Karis on Wednesday extended Madise greetings on the election to the post. https://x.com/AlarKaris/status/2095105418603151427?s=20 Congratulations, lle Madise, on your election as the next President of Estonia. Parliament has made its choice, and I will soon hand over the office to you. Serving as head of state is a great honour and an even greater responsibility. I wish you strength, wisdom and resolve, he said. https://praguemonitor.com/work-life/how-.text: Czechia Business Prague Housing Europe & World Work & Life Briefings Key points A non-EU spouse of a non-EU resident usually applies for a long-term residence permit for family reunification, filed at a Czech embassy, with the Ministry of the Interior deciding. Plan around the slow documents: the marriage certificate with an apostille or legalisation, sworn Czech translations, a criminal-record extract and proof of accommodation and insurance. Spouses of Czech or EU citizens follow different, usually lighter, tracks; check which one applies before you collect paperwork. On this page 5 sections First, which track is your spouse on The documents Filing and the interview After arrival When the marriage is not the issue The applications that fail are rarely the ones with a doubtful marriage. They are the ones where the marriage certificate was issued in one spelling and the passport carries another, where the lease says one bedroom for four people, or where the translator's stamp is missing. A family permit is a document-assembly exercise, and the assembly takes longer than the romance. The Foreigners Act (Act No. 326/1999 Coll.) and the Ministry's lists of documents change; always use the current list for your case. First, which track is your spouse on Before you order any document, work out the sponsor's status, because it decides the track. The wider picture is in our explainer on how family reunification works . In short: If you are a Czech citizen , your non-EU spouse is currently treated much like the family member of an EU citizen: a temporary residence permit and a residence card from the Ministry of the Interior (OAMP), with a path to permanent residence on favourable terms. A bill for a new Foreigners Act, planned for 2029, would tighten this (as of October 2026; check MV). If you are an EU citizen living in Czechia, your non-EU spouse has a right under EU law and obtains a residence card for a family member of an EU citizen. If you are a non-EU national with a long-term or permanent residence permit, your spouse applies for a permit for family reunification, subject to the sponsor's conditions. The general rule is that the sponsor has lived in Czechia for at least 15 months and both spouses are at least 20; Blue Card, intra-company transfer and researcher permits are exempt from the waiting period, and a shorter period is described for employee card holders (as of 2026; check MV/OAMP). The rest of this guide assumes the last case, which has the longest document list, but most of the paperwork applies to all three. The documents The Ministry publishes the exact list; the following describes what it usually contains and what causes problems. Application form and travel document. The form is filled in Czech or English as the Ministry directs, and the passport must be valid beyond the planned stay, with pages free. A passport that expires within months will be questioned. Photographs. Passport-style photographs to the required format. Photo studios near embassies know the specification. Proof of the marriage. A marriage certificate issued by the authority of the country where the marriage took place. For use in Czechia the certificate generally needs an apostille, if the issuing country belongs to the Hague Apostille Convention, or consular legalisation if not, and a sworn translation into Czech. Our guides to apostille and legalisation and sworn translations explain both steps. If your marriage was registered in an EU country, the EU rules on public documents may remove the apostille requirement for some documents; ask the Ministry whether this applies. Proof of accommodation. A tenancy contract or ownership documents showing that the family has a place to live, with the owner's consent where you rent. The Ministry checks that the flat is large enough; the contract should name the address, the tenant and the intended occupants. See renting a flat in Czechia as a foreigner . Proof of health insurance. Your spouse needs insurance that meets the Foreigners Act's requirements from arrival. For most family members this means a commercial policy for foreigners until they are covered by the public system. Check the policy against the Ministry's requirements before paying, and read our guide to health insurance for foreigners . Proof of means. Evidence that the household can live without public assistance: payslips, an employment contract, tax records or bank statements for the sponsor. The Ministry sets the benchmark. Criminal-record extract. For applicants over 15, an extract from the country of citizenship and, on request, from countries where your spouse spent more than six months in the last three years, with an apostille or legalisation and a sworn translation. Like most supporting documents it should be no older than 180 days when filed, or less if the certificate states a shorter validity (as of 2026; check MV). See how to get a criminal-record certificate . Assembling the application Confirm the track and the waiting period Check the sponsor's status and whether any minimum period of residence applies before you book. Order the slow documents first Request the marriage certificate and criminal-record extract, then arrange apostilles. Get the translations done last A sworn translator works from the final, authenticated version, so do not translate before the apostille. Prepare the Czech side Secure the tenancy contract with the owner's consent, the sponsor's income proof and the insurance. Book the embassy appointment File in person, give biometric data and keep the receipt. Filing and the interview The application for a family member who is abroad generally starts at a Czech embassy or consulate in the country where your spouse lives or is legally staying. Appointments are booked online and can be scarce in some cities, so book as soon as your documents are close to ready. At the appointment, the applicant files the form and documents, gives fingerprints and a photograph, and pays the fee. The embassy forwards the file to the Ministry of the Interior, which decides. The Ministry may ask additional questions or request further documents, and it may invite the applicant or the sponsor for an interview, in person or at an embassy, to confirm that the marriage is genuine. Questions concern how you met, daily routines, family members and shared plans. A hypothetical couple who have been married for years and has photographs, travel records and shared bills will find the interview easy. A hypothetical couple who married recently, live in separate countries and have little shared history should expect more questions and prepare documents that show a real relationship. After approval the embassy tells the applicant to collect a visa or to travel, and a residence card is issued after arrival. The details depend on the procedure; ask the embassy what to expect. Once your spouse is in Czechia, they must report their place of stay (see registering your address ), and later address changes of a permit holder go to the Ministry. Names must match A spouse whose surname differs between the passport, marriage certificate and birth certificate should bring a document that explains it, such as a name-change certificate. Mismatches are a common cause of requests for supplementary documents. After arrival A spouse with a long-term permit for family reunification generally has free access to the labour market, so no separate work permit, but confirm the rule for the permit type on the Ministry's page. Health insurance continues to matter: if your spouse takes a job with a Czech employer, public insurance follows from the employment, while a non-working spouse should keep suitable cover. For the sponsor's own permit, see employee cards and Blue Cards . For taxes, social insurance and benefits for the family, see our explainers on Czech social security and maternity and parental benefits . The permit has an expiry date. Renewing it requires the sponsor to maintain their status, accommodation and means, and a mismatch between the family's and the sponsor's dates can cause trouble. Plan renewals together: see how to renew a Czech residence permit . When the marriage is not the issue Some applications run into problems that have nothing to do with the relationship: a sponsor who changed jobs without notifying the Ministry, a flat that was sublet without the owner's agreement, an insurance policy that excludes pre-existing conditions required by the Act, or a criminal-record extract that lapsed while the file waited. Each can be fixed with notice. The expensive mistake is to wait for the Ministry to find it. If the application is refused, the decision states the reasons and the period for appeal. Do not file again without understanding the reason. An immigration lawyer or an organisation that helps foreigners can read the decision with you. Frequently asked questions Where does my spouse apply? Usually at a Czech embassy or consulate in the country where they live. Some cases can be filed in Czechia; check the Ministry of the Interior. Does my marriage certificate need an apostille? Generally an apostille or legalisation, plus a sworn Czech translation. Some EU documents are exempt from the apostille; ask the Ministry. Can my spouse work while the permit is processed? Not until the permit is issued, unless another basis allows it. Once issued, a family permit generally allows work. How long does it take? The statutory limit for a family reunification permit is up to 270 days, shorter for Blue Card families (as of 2026; check MV). Do not book non-refundable travel before approval. This is a general explainer, not legal or tax advice. https://hmh.org/event/film-screening-of-.text: Get tickets Donate Accessibility EN EN ES EVENTS Film Screening of Among Neighbors – Special Event Release Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a reception and film screening of Among Neighbors – Special Event Release in partnership with the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Combining magical realism with traditional documentary techniques, Among Neighbors examines the mystery of a small, rural town where people of two different faiths lived side by side for centuries — until the killing began. The film reveals both love and betrayal as it zeroes in on a crime committed among neighbors: the murder of Holocaust survivors in Poland, six months after the end of World War II. The chilling facts revealed in this documentary have led the office of Poland’s nationalist president to call for a ban on the film. The Special Event Release includes 25 minutes of additional content in the form of a brief introduction by filmmaker Yoav Potash, and an in-depth post-film Q&A compilation that reveals the fascinating making-of stories––as well as the ongoing controversy––behind this critically-acclaimed film. This event is free and open to the public but advanced registration is required. Parking is not included but can be paid following the event. The program includes a reception with lite bites and beverages at 5:30 PM with the film screening scheduled for 6 PM. This screening is funded in part by the MFAH World Faiths Initiative, which is made possible by a grant from Lilly Endowment Inc.
